FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A32
Age alone should not decide whether someone keeps driving, but changes in vision, fitness and reflexes can raise safety concerns, so drivers should assess them and adjust habits or choose other transportation. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A32
Every new driver must pass two exams: the Driving Knowledge Exam, which checks understanding of Washington's rules of the road, and the Driving Skills Exam, which checks the ability to apply them. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A32
The knowledge exam must be passed first, and from that point you have two years to complete the skills exam. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A33
During the skills exam only you and the examiner may ride in the vehicle, with exceptions made for service animals and sign language interpreters. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A33
The skills-exam vehicle must be legally licensed and registered, carry proof of current liability insurance naming the policy holder or describing the vehicle, and have working brake lights, signal lights and seat belts. [A33]
Why it matters: the examiner verifies every requirement before the exam begins, so a burnt-out bulb can stop the test.
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A33
You can take the exams either at an approved driver training school exam location or by booking a driver licensing office appointment in License Express. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A34
Approved driver training for new drivers under 18 combines classroom lessons with behind-the-wheel training from a licensed instructor, offered by private schools and some school districts. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A34
Drivers over 18 who never took driver training face a higher crash risk, so some schools run adult traffic safety courses for beginners, newcomers to the United States, or anyone wanting a refresher. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A35
Driver training courses for students under 18 must offer a parent orientation class that explains the requirement of 40 daylight hours and 10 night hours of practice driving. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A35
A lost, stolen, destroyed or unreadable license can be replaced online at dol.wa.gov, or as a duplicate in person at any driver licensing office. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A35
Your expiration date is near the bottom of the license, and you may renew as early as one year before it expires, online through License Express or at a licensing office. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A35
Renewing after expiration may add a fee, and a license that has been expired 8 or more years means retaking both the skills and knowledge exams. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A36
Grounds for losing driving privileges include breaking intermediate restrictions, a minor possessing alcohol, drugs or firearms, piling up moving violations, and driving while suspended or revoked. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A36
Privileges can also be lost for fleeing police, driving under the influence, racing or reckless driving, endangering a construction or emergency worker, or letting traffic citations go unresolved. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A36
Vehicular assault, vehicular homicide, hit and run, a felony involving a vehicle, driving uninsured, and failing a competency evaluation are further grounds for losing privileges. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A36
A minor who commits an alcohol, drug or firearm offense risks having the license delayed until age 17. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A36
To get a license back you must retake the knowledge and skills exams even if you passed them before, pay a reissue fee on top of the usual fees, and, if under 18, have a parent or guardian's consent. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A37
Washington law, RCW 46.61.502, makes it illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A37
Under RCW 46.61.503 the DUI law also covers being in physical control of a vehicle, even a parked one, which means being able to take control of its engine or operation. [A37]
Why it matters: a common mistake is believing the car must be moving for a DUI to apply.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A37
Under the Implied Consent Law, RCW 46.20.308, anyone who drives in Washington has agreed to be tested whenever an officer suspects alcohol or drug impairment. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A37
A blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher is DUI for drivers aged 21 and older, while drivers under 21 face the same consequences at 0.02%. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A37
More than 5 nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood is DUI for drivers aged 21 and older, while drivers under 21 face the same consequences for anything above 0 nanograms. [A37]
Why it matters: learners often apply the adult cannabis limit to younger drivers, who have no allowance at all.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A37
Refusing a test can cost your driving privilege for 90 to 730 days or until you turn 21, whichever is longer, with the length depending on factors such as how many violations you have. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A38
The guide's limits table lists adults at a BAC of 0.08% or more and THC of 5.00 ng or more, and minors under 21 at a BAC of 0.02% or more and THC above 0.00 ng. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A38
Alcohol and drug offenses stay on your driving record for life, and a DUI arrest can bring license loss, heavy fines, criminal penalties, jail time and higher insurance rates. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A38
A DUI conviction can combine a suspension of 90 days to 4 years with a probationary license, an ignition interlock device, proof of financial responsibility, and an alcohol assessment and treatment report. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A38
A DUI conviction can also require you to reapply for a license, retake the knowledge and skills tests, and pay the reissue fee. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A38
The open container law makes it a traffic infraction for anyone in a vehicle on the road to drink alcohol or use cannabis, hold opened or partly used alcohol or cannabis, or hide either in unlabeled or mislabeled containers. [A38]
Why it matters: the rule covers every occupant, not just the driver.
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A39
Opened alcohol or cannabis may be carried only in the trunk or a truck bed, never in a storage compartment the driver can reach. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A39
After a move you must update your address in License Express within 10 days, but a name change has to be made at a driver licensing office. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A39
You can register to vote at sos.wa.gov or at a licensing office, and residents aged 16 and 17 may pre-register when they apply for a license or ID card. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A39
When applying for a license or ID card you may register with the U.S. Selective Service System and may say whether you are a twin for the state research registry. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

Glossary: reissue fee — the extra charge to get a license back after losing it [A36]. Physical control — being able to operate a vehicle's engine or controls, even when parked [A37]. Implied consent — the agreement every Washington driver makes to be tested when impairment is suspected [A37]. BAC — blood alcohol concentration [A37].
Memory aid: the adult alcohol line of 0.08% is four times the under-21 line of 0.02% [A37].
